final.title: Measure memory where the workflow actually needs it
final.body:
If you are asking about agent memory, the useful question is not “can it remember?” but “does this workflow need it?” For a small business owner, that matters only when the same system must carry context forward across separate interactions: a customer asks on Monday, replies on Wednesday, and the agent still needs to understand the earlier request without you pasting the whole thread back in.

That is the bounded decision for a pilot. Do not try to measure memory in the abstract. Pick one recurring workflow and define one observable test: does the agent correctly reference a prior preference, instruction, or open issue without being re-fed the full history? If it cannot, you have learned something practical. If every request arrives complete and self-contained, memory may simply not be the thing to pay for.

The diagnostic question is simple: are your repeated tasks truly stateful, or are they just repetitive? “Stateful” means later steps depend on earlier ones; “repetitive” means each request already contains enough context on its own.

One practical next step: write down one real recurring interaction and the exact pieces of information that must carry forward. Then keep that as the pilot scope. That keeps memory testing tied to a workflow, not to a slogan.
